regeln: Align every visual motif with the specific entity, product, or action named in narration; never use generic handshakes or office workers as fillers.
Use authentic screenshots, dashboard views, or production scenes when the script mentions digital tools, apps, or manufacturing processes.
Center the main subject or evidence prominently; avoid empty vertical space, tiny repeated photos, or background-only frames.
Maintain format-specific pacing: Shorts require 3-5 second distinct shots; long videos allow longer demonstrations with pivots every 40-60 seconds.
Open Shorts hooks instantly with recognizable entity names, key figures, or the central business conflict.
Preserve the original painted-world style and established presenter identities; introduce figures early and vary their actions.
Explicitly bridge pivots in business models or product shifts to maintain narrative logic during historical transitions.
Translate complex financial metrics into simple comparative language paired with clear, aligned visual demonstrations.
Include mandatory spoken like, share, and save calls at format-specific positions (after stakes in Shorts; after payoffs in long videos).
Adhere strictly to source-backed facts and approved channel voices; do not add unverified claims or speculative metrics.
Treat feedback as data for habit improvement; do not over-generalize one image defect into a ban on an entire style.
Verify channel archives before production to avoid topic duplication and ensure visual consistency across the series.
